claim: Airla et al. reported peripheral blood immune-system gene suppression after methylprednisolone treatment during multiple sclerosis exacerbations.
future_grounding_route: Use as source-specific steroid transcriptome context for future construction or validation of glucocorticoid-response confounder panels; do not use as evidence that the V22 scalar survives steroid adjustment.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: V22 scalar is immune-tone bounded, not steroid/composition artifact

project_use: Sharper V50 source record supporting why glucocorticoid-response signatures are a required confounder panel in treatment-response validation.
relationship_note: This source supports steroid transcriptome confounding as a real concern in MS blood expression studies, but it does not test the locked V22 scalar or the V32 adjustment result.

source.citation: Airla N, Luomala M, Elovaara I, Kettunen E, Knuutila S, Lehtimaki T. Suppression of immune system genes by methylprednisolone in exacerbations of multiple sclerosis. Journal of Neurology. 2004;251:1215-1219.
source.label: Airla 2004 methylprednisolone MS immune-gene suppression

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Springer article page; metadata-only reuse in V50
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores source metadata and a short paraphrased claim only.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the Airla et al. expression data or mapped it to the frozen V32 glucocorticoid confounder panel.
